newsitem.title: MALI: Mali police out in force before banned march.
newsitem.headline: Mali police out in force before banned march.

text.p: Police were out in force in Mali's capital Bamako on Wednesday after the government banned all street protests ahead of a planned opposition demonstration to demand that elections be suspended.

Witnesses said small groups of opposition militants made their way towards the capital's Place de la Liberte square, focus of protests during the pro-democracy demonstrations that helped topple dictator Moussa Traore in 1991.

Two opposition alliances urged their supporters to turn out in force on Wednesday to demonstrate their rejection of Sunday's parliamentary election during which severe organisational problems prevented many people voting.
Territorial Administration and Security Minister Lieutenant-Colonel Sada Samake banned all street protests in a statement issued on Tuesday.

Sunday's poll for a new 147-seat parliament and presidential and municipal elections in May and June are a test of how deeply democracy has taken root in Mali, which won widespread praise for its 1992 democratic transition from military dictatorship.

Voters turned out in force for the election, which launched the impoverished nation's second multi-party national polls since independence from France in 1960. They cited problems with voter cards and electoral lists and lack of voting materials.
The opposition alliances, who say they will boycott the remaining elections, have also demanded the resignation of President Alpha Oumar Konare's government.

Konare, a historian elected in 1992, had been due to face nine challengers in a May 4 presidential poll. He has steered Mali on a course of economic liberalisation, winning praise from the United States and the World Bank.
